rationale: Ninety-third pass: consolidate the witness guard as one statement across the client entry points rather than one path at a time. The read path was just traced; checking the others shows the same shape in each: the command proposal, the session proposal, the configuration change, the snapshot request and the leader-transfer request all test for an uninitialized node and then reject a witness with the invalid-operation error before creating or queueing any request state or offering anything to raft. Only after those checks does each path touch its pending-proposal, pending-configuration, pending-snapshot or leader-transfer object. Recording that as a single Fact gives the audit one citable statement about role enforcement, and it explains why the raft-layer witness branch examined in the previous pass is defence in depth: the layer that could leave a caller to its deadline is never reached by an in-tree client.

knowledge.statement: Each client-facing operation entry point on a node refuses work on a witness before any request state exists. The command proposal and the session proposal both check initialization and then return the invalid-operation error for a witness before touching the pending proposal map; the read entry point does the same before obtaining read request state; the configuration-change entry point rejects a witness before creating a pending configuration change; the snapshot request entry point rejects a witness before it decides between a user-requested and an exported snapshot or reaches the pending snapshot object; and the leader-transfer entry point rejects a witness before offering a target to the leader-transfer channel. In every case the check is on the node's own witness configuration rather than on its applied membership, and the caller receives the invalid-operation error synchronously, so no request is left waiting for a deadline or for a raft-layer rejection to be reported. The raft layer keeps its own witness-specific refusals as defence in depth, including the ReadIndex branch that logs without reporting.
knowledge.conditions: A client calls a node-level proposal, session proposal, read, configuration-change, snapshot or leader-transfer entry point on a node whose configuration marks it as a witness; the node is initialized so the witness check rather than the readiness check decides the outcome.
